paper_id: Dong et al. - 2014 - Elon Enabling efficient and long-term reprogramming for wireless sensor networks
title: Elon: Enabling Efficient and Long-Term Reprogramming for Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: WSN nodes deployed in forests/vast areas are physically inaccessible; existing reprogramming protocols waste energy transmitting large kernels and suffer reboot-induced outages.
problem_framing: Three orthogonal bottlenecks: (1) transferred code size, (2) reboot cost (state loss), (3) flash-write voltage floor limiting reprogrammable lifetime to first 23% of battery life.
key_insight: TinyOS kernel changes slowly while application changes fast; by annotating replaceable vs. system components, disseminate only the delta—making the common case fast.
method_signature: Compiler-extended annotations, two-phase linking, system jump table indirection, partial reboot avoiding kernel-state loss.
evaluation_criteria: Transferred code size reduction, beacon packet overhead for state recovery, reprogrammable lifetime extension (3.3× TelosB).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Elon trades flexibility: needs code annotations upfront; cannot update kernel components without full image; Mica/Harvard-architecture nodes lose lifetime benefit.
evidence_for_taste: the TinyOS kernel components are slowly changing while the application component is quickly changing
the voltage of some nodes quickly falls below 2.7V
reboots from a software error led to 3-day network outage
thinking_moves: 把系统划分为稳态kernel和动态replaceable两部分，只传变动的部分
利用Von Neumann架构把代码放RAM，避免flash write的电压约束
借鉴microreboot思想，设计partial reboot保留kernel状态表
把annotation成本作为工程代价接受，换性能收益
cites_own_work: GreenOrbs (Mo et al. 2009) is the real-world complex application motivating the design
